findings.title: Unpinned package executed on every start: mcp-server-robinhood-chain
findings.detail: 'mcp-server-robinhood-chain' launches mcp-server-robinhood-chain through npx without a version. The client resolves the version at start time, so any future publish to that package name runs with your credentials. This is how postmark-mcp (Sept 2025) reached roughly 300 organisations.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version and an integrity hash: "args": ["mcp-server-robinhood-chain@<version>"] and drop the -y flag. Re-pin deliberately, after reviewing the diff.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=1.00): rhc_equities
findings.detail: The description of 'mcp-server-robinhood-chain.rhc_equities' scores 1.00 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: encoded_blob. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: encoded_blob, cross_tool, entropy, log_len.

evidence.description: Robinhood Chain tokenized equities — every official Robinhood tokenized stock and ETF (NVDA, SPY, AAPL, …) with live price / market cap / liquidity and 24h trades, ETH volume, buys/sells and distinct buyers/sellers. IDENTITY IS THE ISSUER BEACON, NEVER THE NAME: a token is listed only if its contract is an EIP-1967 beacon proxy on Robinhood's issuer beacon 0xe10b6f6b275de231345c20d14ab812db62151b00, read from our own node (re-classified every 10 min). evidence.description: EVM-native risk assessment for a Robinhood Chain token, computed LIVE against a self-hosted RHC node. THIS IS NOT THE SOLANA RISK MODEL: EVM has no mint or freeze authority. Across 300 random RHC tokens only 2.3% even expose an owner() function and 0% expose mint in their own bytecode — so an ABSENT capability flag is the NORM and is NOT a safety signal. findings.title: Toxic flow within 'mcp-server-robinhood-chain': executes commands + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 34 combination(s) exist where one tool executes commands and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they executes commands and can reach the network, which is remote code execution with a delivery channel rather than a hint of one. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'mcp-server-robinhood-chain': reads credentials or secrets + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 9 combination(s) exist where one tool reads credentials or secrets and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they reads credentials and can send data to an address it controls. A single prompt is enough to turn 'summarise this config' into a credential leak. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'mcp-server-robinhood-chain': reads credentials or secrets + sends email or messages
findings.detail: 2 combination(s) exist where one tool reads credentials or secrets and another sends email or messages. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they reads credentials and can send mail. This is the postmark-mcp shape: the mail tool was legitimate, the credentials were reachable, and the combination was the incident. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.

findings.title: No baseline supplied - drift detection is disabled
findings.detail: Without an approved snapshot the scanner cannot tell a tool that has always been there from one that appeared yesterday. The single most effective MCP control is the diff, and it needs a baseline to diff against.
findings.remediation: Run 'mcp-scrutiny baseline --config <file> --out mcp-baseline.json', commit the file, and pass it back with --baseline on every later scan.
